column1: # *** WHY THE TRINIDAD LERENAS NEEDED DISPENSING - ANSWERED BY A BIRTH ACT. 9 October 2026. ***
# *** Flores, Birth Records 1887-1901 *** - image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-333J-F, found by full-text search.
# *** Entry No. 10, CAYETANO ALBERTO FERNANDEZ ***, born at PINTOS on 7 August 1897 and registered on
# the 14th before Elisco D. Dogniño, Juez de Paz of the Santa section of Flores.
# *** A URUGUAYAN CIVIL BIRTH ACT NAMES ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS WITH THEIR AGES, TRADES AND ADDRESSES.
# *** That is why this one entry does more than the nine dispensations of yesterday put together.

column2: *** Don SERAPIO FERNANDEZ ***, forty-one, married, oriental, *** HACENDADO ***, vecino de *** CERRO COLORADO ***
column3: Born about *** 1856 ***. He is the groom of the dispensation of *** 26 June 1885 ***.

column2: *** Dona ANTONINA LERENA ***, oriental, *** thirty-five ***, married, de profesion labores, living with her husband
column3: Born about *** 1862 ***. She is the bride of that dispensation - and *** SHE IS NOT THE ANTONINA LERENA OF THE 1880 MARRIAGE ACT ***, who was already the mother of a thirty-year-old. *** THERE ARE TWO WOMEN OF THIS NAME AT TRINIDAD *** and this archive must not collapse them.

column1: *** HER PARENTS - AND THIS IS THE FIND ***
column2: por linea materna de *** Don BERNABE LERENA ***, Oriental, de *** sesenta y dos anos ***, casado, de profesion *** hacendado *** y vecino de *** CERRO COLORADO ***, y de *** Dona CASIMIRA PELAEZ ***, Oriental, de *** cincuenta y seis anos ***, casada, de profesion labores
column3: *** ANTONINA IS A DAUGHTER OF BERNABE LERENA AND CASIMIRA PELAEZ *** - the Trinidad founding couple this archive has carried since September with *** no ages, no addresses and four children ***. She is a fifth. *** AND BOTH NOW HAVE A BIRTH YEAR: *** Bernabe about *** 1835 ***, Casimira about *** 1841 ***, both at Cerro Colorado in 1897.

column1: *** HIS PARENTS - AND THIS IS THE EXPLANATION ***
column2: por linea paterna de *** Don SERAPIO FERNANDEZ ***, Oriental, *** fallecido ***, y de *** Dona SOCORRO LERENA ***, Oriental, de *** sesenta y cinco anos ***, propietaria y domiciliada en *** TRINIDAD ***
column3: *** THE GROOM'S MOTHER IS A LERENA TOO. *** Socorro Lerena, born about *** 1832 ***, a widow and a property owner at Trinidad - *** a woman entirely new to this archive. ***

column1: *** WHY THEY HAD TO BE DISPENSED ***
column2: The Archbishop lifted *** the SECOND grade of consanguinity by the EQUAL lateral line *** before this couple could marry in 1885
column3: *** THE ACT SUPPLIES THE MECHANISM THE DISPENSATION ONLY IMPLIED. *** He descends from a Lerena through his mother SOCORRO; she descends from a Lerena through her father BERNABE. *** IF SOCORRO AND BERNABE ARE BROTHER AND SISTER, THE COUPLE ARE FIRST COUSINS *** - which is exactly what an equal second degree means. *** THAT IS INFERRED AND NOT PROVED: *** Socorro's own parents are not named here, and no record yet joins her to Bernabe. *** What the act DOES prove is that Lerena blood runs down both sides of this marriage. ***

column1: *** AND A LERENA-PELAEZ UNION A GENERATION EARLIER ***
column2: *** Santisima Trinidad, Religious Marriage Records 1875-1895 ***, 6 March 1880: Don Rafael Sanchez, widower, married *** MARIA PELAEZ, thirty, hija legitima de Don JUAN PELAEZ y de Dona ANTONINA LERENA *** - and *** Dona Antonina Lerena was a witness at her own daughter's wedding ***, with Don Balbino Pelaez
column3: *** THE ELDER ANTONINA. *** A daughter of thirty in 1880 puts this Antonina's own birth near *** 1830 ***. *** SO A LERENA MARRIED A PELAEZ AROUND 1845 ***, and Bernabe Lerena married another Peláez a generation later. *** THAT IS WHY THE 1885, 1894 AND 1913 COUPLES WERE ALL COUSINS: *** two families had been marrying each other for two generations, and by the third the Church had to compute the degrees.
